newsitem.title: UK: EMU expectations mostly higher - JP Morgan index.
newsitem.headline: EMU expectations mostly higher - JP Morgan index.

text.p: Market expectations of a broad-based European monetary union were mostly stronger or unchanged over the past week but the probability of Sweden and Britain taking part slipped slightly, according to JP Morgan's EMU calculator.

In the past five trading days, market prices indicate that the perceived probability of Sweden joining EMU in 1999 has receded by two percentage points to 76 percent, while that for Britain edged down by one point to 42.
The market still believes there is a 100 percent chance of France and Belgium joining in 1999, which was the same as last week.
Spain still had the highest probability among the other nations, with the figure edging up one percentage point to 83 percent. Probabilities for Italy and Denmark also rose slightly.

JP Morgan's EMU calculator derives from the interest rate swaps market probabilities of individual countries joining Germany in EMU in 1999. The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
